text:
laura: Heads up — after the role-id shard flip this morning we're seeing a short spike of 403s from the batch-ingest service during the canary window. Noticed ~3-4% errors for write paths. Anyone else seeing this?

mike: saw a handful in logs, sampling now. Likely mapping mismatch between old role_id and new role_uuid.

samir: confirming — audit logs show principal `svc-batch` trying to hit `ingest:write` but DB denies because `role_uuid` lookup returned null.

rohan: deploy-bot shows the migration job finished at 07:12 UTC and canary started at 07:15. Could be a caching layer still pointing at old ids.

deploy-bot: migration-job-17233 finished successfully (duration 3m21s). Canary rollout step=1/3.

laura: @samir can you attach a sample log line? need to confirm whether this is a read-after-write index issue or missing default alias.

samir: sample: `ts=2026-03-20T07:18:11Z svc=svc-batch user=svc-batch req=/v1/items method=POST err=403 role_lookup=null`

mike: quick fix option: temporary alias table mapping old_role_id -> new_role_uuid and switch auth lookup to try alias fallback. Should be cheap and reversible.

rohan: agree. I'll put a canary tweak that expands lookup: `SELECT coalesce(role_uuid, alias_map.role_uuid) FROM roles LEFT JOIN alias_map ON roles.old_id = alias_map.old_id` in the auth service.

laura: do it. Keep canary at 10% and watch latency + audit logs. Also check KMS access for the service token — saw an unrelated KMS timeout earlier but might be noisy.

samir: created a tiny migration-to-alias table and pushed to canary cluster. SQL:```
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS role_aliases (old_id text PRIMARY KEY, role_uuid uuid);
INSERT INTO role_aliases VALUES ('role-17', 'a8f3-...');
```

rohan: auth service updated to try alias table, deployed to canary (10%).

sre-bot: alert: 403 rate for svc-batch on canary decreased from 3.9% -> 0.4% in 3 minutes.

mike: nice, looks like fallback helped. Need to validate audit trail for those aliased grants — we must emit both old_id and resolved uuid to logs for later triage.

security-bot: note: audit pipeline detected gaps between 07:12-07:16 for a subset of events (ingest write). Logging retention unaffected but some events lacked role_uuid. Please preserve raw events.

laura: good catch. @samir can we retroactively backfill role_uuid into audit events from the alias table for that interval? Keep it as a safe append-only patch.

samir: yes, can run a backfill job limited to 07:10-07:20 using alias mapping and write corrected entries to the audit_shadow table. Running dry-run now.

rohan: also propose we add a short-term healthcheck: after any role migration, delay canary scale to >0 until auth caches are invalidated OR run cache-invalidate webhook. Prevents read-after-write mismatch.

laura: agreed — add cache-invalidate step to migration playbook and require audit checkpass before ramp. File an infra ticket.

mike: one more: ensure KMS key policy allowed `svc-batch` to decrypt service tokens post-migration. If KMS perms were mis-evaluated via role lookup, that would surface as decrypt errors.

samir: dry-run backfill complete, 0 rows changed (expected small set), ready to apply.

laura: go ahead with backfill and keep canary at 10% for 20m. If 403s stay low we incrementally roll to 50%. If anything spikes, rollback alias fallback and revert auth code.

rohan: rolling forward. I'll add an alert to the runbook: `role-migration: prolonged 403 > 1% for 10m -> pause rollout`.

sre-bot: canary metrics stable. 403s at 0.3%, latency unchanged.

laura: thanks all. After we stabilize, write a short blameless post with timeline and a checklist item for playbook (cache invalidate + audit verification).

mike: 👍 will draft postmortem and add remediation tasks.

security-bot: recorded incident stub: "role id shift -> alias fallback added during canary; audit backfilled".

laura: closing the loop — keep channel updated for final roll to 50% then full. If anyone sees other anomalies ping here. :thumbsup:
